title: さて — now then / well then
summary: A conjunction or filler used to change the topic or move to the next action: “now then, well then.” It marks a turning point in a speech, a letter or a conversation. Often used when starting a task or the main subject.

patterns.gloss: start of a new topic or action (さて、始めましょう)

body.p: As in 準備ができました。さて、出発しましょうか, it is used after a pause to move on. In speech it also works as a switch-over cue before getting started (さて、そろそろ始めましょう). It is handy in meetings, classes and presentations to shift the flow.

It is close to では and それでは, but さて has a stronger feel of shifting gears in your own mind. In letters and emails, it often opens the main business after greetings: さて、〜の件ですが. For a topic completely unrelated to the previous one, use ところで.

examples.ja: さて、そろそろ始（はじ）めましょう。
準備（じゅんび）ができました。さて、出発（しゅっぱつ）しましょうか。
examples.romaji: Junbi ga dekimashita. Sate, shuppatsu shimashō ka.
examples.tr: We're ready. Now then, shall we set off?
examples.note: Moving to the next action after a pause.

examples.ja: さて、次（つぎ）の話題（わだい）に移（うつ）りたいと思（おも）います。
examples.romaji: Sate, tsugi no wadai ni utsuritai to omoimasu.
examples.tr: Well then, I'd like to move on to the next topic.
examples.note: Changing the topic in a talk.

pitfalls: For a totally unrelated change of subject use ところで. さて marks a break within the flow.
Put it at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma, not in the middle.
